title: Schedule updates accept invalid time zones but silently run them in UTC

evidence.quote:
if payload.timezone is not None:
        sched.timezone = payload.timezone

update_resp = client.put(
        f"/api/podcast/schedules/{schedule_id}",
        json={"name": "Morning Briefing", "days": ["monday", "tuesday"], "time": "08:00"},
        headers=auth_headers,
    )

reasoning: The PUT route persists any non-null timezone string without checking that it is an IANA timezone. The scheduler later catches UnknownTimeZoneError and runs the schedule in UTC while the API continues returning the invalid stored timezone. A client can therefore receive a 200 response for a schedule that appears configured for one timezone but executes at a different time basis, which is a user-visible scheduling correctness and API contract bug.
reproduction: Create a schedule, then PUT /api/podcast/schedules/{id} with {"timezone":"Not/AZone"}. The update succeeds and stores Not/AZone; when scheduler jobs are rebuilt, that schedule is configured with UTC instead.
recommendation: Validate payload.timezone in update_podcast_schedule_endpoint before committing, using zoneinfo.ZoneInfo or pytz.timezone, and return 400 for unknown timezone names. Apply the same validation to schedule creation for consistency.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The schedule update coverage only exercises name/days/time/enabled updates and creation validation only checks empty days and invalid time; there is no invalid timezone case.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an API test that creates a schedule, sends PUT /api/podcast/schedules/{id} with an invalid timezone, asserts 400, and verifies the previously stored timezone remains unchanged.
minimumFixScope: Add timezone validation in app/api/podcast.py for PodcastScheduleUpdate.timezone, ideally shared with create_podcast_schedule to keep create and update behavior aligned.
